A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with readable main text, equations, figures, and tables. However, both end with references and omit the appendices they cite, including v3's Appendices D/E. Main-paper comparison is reliable, but appendix-dependent implementation details cannot be compared.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and real-image denoising experiments, cross-instrument evaluations, and component and calibration-frame ablations in Tables 3–5 and Figure 10.

after.justification: v3 reports original denoising experiments and ablations, including newly reported flux-recovery results from mock PSFs injected into real observations.

M1.justification: The noise components, distribution models, U-Net architecture, and Raw-L1 objective remain unchanged. Section 4 replaces 'register and average' with 'stack,' but unregistered averaging was already described in v1's abstract and introduction; an actual change to base-image construction is not established.

E1.justification: v3 introduces a controlled scenario using known-flux mock PSFs injected into real observations. The underlying MuSCAT-3/MuSCAT-4 datasets, three evaluated bands, and cross-instrument denoising task remain; revised sample counts do not establish broader dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Drizzle has real-image PSNR results in v1's Tables 3–4 but no results in v3's replacement FLUX-SNR comparison, although its background-noise results remain. Other comparator membership is unchanged. Table 4's NCOH-to-NMOH spelling correction identifies the same cited method.

E3.justification: Real-data fidelity evaluation changes from PSNR/SSIM against calibrated references to FLUX-SNR against injected mock-source ground truth, including the ablations. Table 1 also revises sample counts: MuSCAT-3 G' training/testing counts change from 152/36 to 215/54, alongside calibration and processed-image count revisions. These reported changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The same five component-removal tests and calibration-frame sensitivity studies remain. Table 5 replaces reference-based PSNR/SSIM evidence with mock-PSF flux recovery, and Figure 10(a,b) replaces PSNR curves with FLUX-SNR curves. These revise evidence for existing diagnostic questions without adding new ablated components.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. NMAD and STD remain spatial background-noise metrics rather than uncertainty estimates across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 replace real-image PSNR outcomes with FLUX-SNR results, with Ours averaging 40.63 and 40.83 dB. Average leaders change from N2N/PMN under the old metric to Ours under the new protocol; this is not a same-setting performance gain. Synthetic PSNR and main background scores remain unchanged. Ablation results also change, including G' NMAD without read noise from 2.33 to 2.38.

T1.justification: The CCD formation equations and probability models retain their mathematical substance. The quantization formula moves inline, and the hot-pixel equation is renumbered. No new proof, derivation, or formal definition accompanies the new evaluation metric.

C1.justification: The noise-model and dataset contributions remain. Unregistered averaging loses its standalone contribution bullet but remains described. A new contribution bullet emphasizes photometric and scientific accuracy, and the conclusion broadens superiority claims from recent learning-based approaches to baseline approaches generally.

C2.justification: Interpretation shifts from fitting noisy calibrated references toward flux preservation, adding explanations involving overlooked CCD/PRNU characteristics and fixed-pattern overlap with mock PSFs. v1's explicit limitation concerning evaluation on only two MuSCAT instruments and the need for broader validation is omitted; difficulty obtaining real ground truth remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: The main text adds code-access information and omits CCD model/passband specifications while retaining training hyperparameters. However, both versions refer implementation details to appendices absent from the supplied PDFs, particularly v3's Appendices D/E. The full extent of reproducibility-detail changes therefore cannot be established.

R1.justification: v3 adds Guo et al. on astronomical spatiotemporal denoising, Jiang et al. on EMCCD noise modeling, and Pan et al. on lunar-image denoising, while removing NeRF in the Dark. These provide limited contextual and evaluation-method support without substantially restructuring the research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, evaluation discussion, and ablation explanations are revised, with localized shortening elsewhere. The main section sequence remains intact. Author and affiliation information also changes, including the addition of Quanfeng Xu.

P2.justification: The existing figure/table framework remains, with relocated displays, revised metric columns in Tables 3–5, and redrawn axes and curves in Figure 10(a,b). Figure 8 replaces the I'-band V1298-Tau example with an R'-band WASP-53 example, although Section 5.2 still calls it I'-band.

improvement.justification: Mock-PSF flux recovery in Tables 3–5 provides more direct evidence of signal preservation than v1's comparison against acknowledged noisy references. This supports a limited quality improvement. The benefit is constrained by unspecified FLUX-SNR and injection details in the supplied PDFs, unavailable appendices, and the removal of explicit generalization limitations while superiority claims broaden.
